chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In regards to a woman who dies before her husband or a man before his wife, he said: Whatever of the possessions which [conventionally] belong to women then it is for the wife, and whatever of the possessions which [conventionally] belong to both men and women then it is to be divided between them

key_terms.بَيْنَهُمَا: between the two (referring to the two estates/spouses)

ai.seo_question: How is marital property divided if one spouse dies before the other according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the division of marital assets by distinguishing between exclusive personal property and joint possessions, a principle rooted in the Shia understanding of *mahr* and personal wealth. This ruling ensures that items designated for one spouse remain with their estate, while shared goods are equitably distributed, reflecting the jurisprudential emphasis on individual ownership rights within the marital bond.
